narrative_purpose: Capture the chapter's essence at a glance: a huge four-winged predator banking hard out of volcanic ash, its two wing pairs caught moving in opposite directions so the viewer immediately counts four wings and asks why.
subject: An enormous dark six-limbed flying predator seen in three-quarter view, banked steeply onto one side. It has TWO separate pairs of membranous wings: a large front pair sweeping downward and a second, clearly separate rear pair sweeping upward on the opposite beat. A long hard bone horn projects forward from the front of its skull. A small blue-skinned Na'vi rider is crouched low against its shoulders, almost lost in the animal's scale.
scene: Inside a drifting column of volcanic ash above dark basalt ridges, grit suspended in the air, the ground far below lost in grey murk, a faint ember-orange glow of lava venting somewhere beneath the haze.
camera: Low three-quarter view looking up at the banked animal, wide enough to show the full wing arrangement, the creature filling the upper two thirds of the frame.
light: Dim ashen daylight from above with a weak warm ember glow rising from below, catching the underside of the wing membranes so the two pairs read as distinct surfaces.
palette: Charcoal, ash-grey and deep crimson on the animal against cool indigo haze; a single restrained ember-amber underglow as the only warm note.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, observed rather than posed action art.
detail_level: Crisp wing membranes, horn and rider; the ash column and ridges dissolving into atmospheric haze.
composition: The banked animal on a strong diagonal across the frame, generous hazy negative space lower left, ridge line low in the far third.
consistency_notes: The animal MUST clearly have two separate pairs of driven wings, the rear pair as fully developed lifting surfaces rather than small tail fins, and the pairs must be caught at opposite points of their stroke. No walking hind legs - the rear limbs are part of the aft wing structure. Forward-projecting bone horn on the skull. Dark charcoal and crimson colouring suited to ash and basalt, not forest.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no green rainforest, no neon glow, no 3D-render or photographic look, no cartoon style, no walking hind legs, no single wing pair
